#1593. Estonia vs Bulgaria - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 14 Nov 2026 23:32, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 02:37

Estonia will welcome Bulgaria to the Lillekula Stadium in Tallinn for Monday's UEFA Nations League encounter.

The hosts, who have secured a top-two finish, could still achieve automatic promotion, while the visitors only have pride to play for on the final matchday of the league phase.

Having been in the bottom two tiers for all five editions of the Nations League, Estonia have put themselves in a position to win promotion to League B for the very first time.

Jurgen Henn's side are guaranteed at least a promotion playoff spot after winning the draw and drawing three of their five matches in Group 4C.

In fact, they have recorded four consecutive shutouts since playing out a 1-1 draw with Iceland on the first matchday.

Their latest clean sheet enabled them to pick up a 1-0 victory in Saturday's away clash against Luxembourg, which came courtesy of Maksim Paskotsi's second goal of the 2026-27 Nations League campaign.

Sitting in second spot and two points adrift of Iceland, Estonia know they need a win and Luxembourg to claim three points in Reykjavik if they are to snatch automatic promotion on the final matchday.

That would require Estonia to pick up their first-ever win against Bulgaria, having drawn two and lost one of their previous three meetings.

Bulgaria already know they will be competing in League C next time around after falling hopelessly short in their promotion bid, mustering just four points from their five matches in Group C4.

After taking just a point from their first three games, Bulgaria finally ended their five-game winless run in all internationals with a 2-0 away victory over Luxembourg in their final outing of the September/October international break.

However, they failed to build upon that result in their most recent outing against Iceland, as they slumped to a demoralising 5-0 defeat in Plovdiv, ensuring they will end the league phase without a home win to their name.

While they cannot finish any higher than third, the Lions are still at risk of dropping to the bottom of the group, with just a point separating them from Luxembourg in fourth position.

Bulgaria may be unbeaten in three meetings against Estonia, but they had to settle for a goalless draw in their only previous away encounter in European Championship qualifying in April 2003.

Their hopes of troubling the scorers on this occasion may be tempered by the fact they have failed to score in three of their last four outings, including a stalemate in September's reverse fixture between these two nations.

Henn could opt for consistency by naming the same lineup that started Friday's narrow win over Luxembourg.

Friday's match-winner Paskotsi will feature alongside Erko Tougjas and Karol Mets in central defence, while Rasmus Peetson and Michael Schjonning-Larsen are set to operate as the two wing-backs.

At the opposite end of the pitch, Patrik Kristal will lead the line with Mattias Mannilaan, who is aiming to bring his club form to the international stage after netting five goals in his last four games for Kalju.

As for the visitors, they are unable to call upon Martin Minchev, who withdrew from the squad last week due to injury.

With Ribarski likely to make alterations, Ivan Turitsov and Dimitar Velkovski are in contention to feature in the backline on Monday.

Martin Petkov, Ivaylo Chochev and Georgi Lazarov are also among those who could come into Ribarski's thinking.

#1592. Report: Bayern Munich sensation now 'extremely high' on Liverpool's shortlist

Liverpool have a lot of issues within their squad that need resolving.

The Anfield outfit may have spent over £150 million trying to improve each area of their team but, they've still ended up fourth in the Premier League table.

Granted, we're only 10 games into the season at the moment but, their performances have seemed to be the same since the start of the campaign.

They seem to be able to easily beat teams who are noticeably weaker than them (aside from Fenerbahce) while they struggle against teams who are noticeably better than them such as Arsenal and Manchester City.

This has made it clear that more talent needs to be added to Liverpool's ranks with another player now entering the mix.

Liverpool have set their eyes on Bayern Munich starlet, Tom Bischof

Midfield and full-back are the two main areas that Liverpool have been lacking in this season.

Indeed, there have been some games when the players in those positions have performed well but, more often than not, they've played well below expectations.

This has led to many different players being linked with an Anfield switch and now, yet another player has entered the equation.

"In addition to Pablo Barrios, Bayern Munich’s Tom Bischof remains extremely high on #LFC’s radar, as reported several weeks ago, with further developments now emerging behind the scenes," ITK Space wrote.

"Liverpool’s scouting department regard the German as one of Europe’s most exceptional emerging midfield talents, with his increasing involvement at Bayern this season only strengthening an already outstanding internal assessment.

"Remarkably, some within the club are understood to rank Bischof even ahead of Pablo Barrios in their internal evaluations, with an exchange of information having already taken place with Germany’s new national team manager Jürgen Klopp, who handed Bischof his senior international debut and is understood to regard him as a cornerstone of Germany’s midfield for the next decade.

"Furthermore, Bischof has already made contact with Florian Wirtz to gain a deeper understanding of life at Liverpool, the atmosphere within the dressing room and the environment surrounding the club, adding another fascinating dimension to a developing story in which Liverpool's admiration extends considerably beyond routine scouting interest."

Tom Bischof is one of the most versatile players that Liverpool can sign

Versatility is one of the most important things that a footballer can have in their locker in this day and age.

The ability to play in multiple positions is not only helpful for the club but, it also means that the player is likely to get more chances to play.

Whether they're used in their preferred position or not is another question but, the fact that most players can now comfortably be used in more than one position is a sign of the times changing.

Bischof is probably a player that most people outside of the Bundesliga wont have heard of but, throughout his career, he's played in almost every position except from striker and centre-back.

Recently, he's honed his skills on three specific positions, left-back, right-back and central midfield.

All three of these positions are where Liverpool need upgrades this term so, signing one player who can cover all three would be huge.

Obviously, change is afoot this January with Liverpool still miles behind their title rivals.

So, if Bischof can be bought, he should definitely be one of the first transfers that Iraola and Julian Ward make, especially because he's only 21 years old and has already featured in 172 games throughout his career.

Liverpool are keen on Lens centre-back Pierre Ismaelo Ganiou despite interest from a number of other clubs, the latest report has claimed.

The Premier League is now on pause for the November international break, and that has given Reds supporters the chance to assess the squad.

Andoni Iraola has made a positive start to life at Anfield, with the team's defence having notably improved, led by the likes of Virgil van Dijk and Ronald Araujo.

However, Van Djik has entered the final year of his contract, while Araujo is only on loan from Barcelona and could return to the Spanish side at the end of the season.

Amid uncertainty regarding the future of their defence, Football Insider report that the Reds are one of several clubs keen on signing Lens defender Ganiou, who is valued by Transfermarkt at just over £25m.

Ganiou does not have an extensive history of top-flight football considering he has played just 28 games in Ligue 1 in his entire career, though he has been impressive for Lens.

In five league matches for the French side this season, the 21-year-old has won 69% of his duels, including 73% of his ground duels.

Liverpool have typically looked to sign aerially dominant defenders, so while the Frenchman boasts an impressive 64% duel success rate in the air, he only averages 1.8 aerial duels won per game.

Van Dijk has won an average of 3.8 duels in the air in the league so far, while Jeremy Jacquet has won 2.6 aerial duels in the Premier League, and the Reds would almost certainly aim to get Ganiou closer to those figures.

Joe Gomez is expected to leave, and he could be replaced in the squad by Araujo, which would then leave the club in need of a right-back.

Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni will be part of the squad for the coming seasons, while many believe that Ifeanyi Ndukwe could play a role for the team once his loan at Levante ends.

#1589. Report: Future of Liverpool sensation unclear, he could be axed

Liverpool have a lot of players within their squad.

However, as has always been the case, certain players are preferred over others.

But, with Andoni Iraola being brought in to replace Arne Slot, some subtle changes were made to the Reds' first-team plans.

For example, if Slot was still in charge, Trey Nyoni, Lewis Koumas and James McConnell would have all been loaned out and forgotten about.

But, with the Spaniard in charge, that has not been the case. Some questions have been raised about what the future holds for certain Liverpool players but, for one sensation, it's still rather unclear.

Valencia could still end up terminating Harvey Elliott's loan early

Harvey Elliott's Liverpool career has been a bit like a rollercoaster.

The Englishman started off his time at Anfield as one of the first names on Jurgen Klopp's team sheet.

Granted, he did spend a season out on loan to Blackburn Rovers but, aside from then, he was often kept in and around Liverpool's starting XI.

However, since Slot and Iraola have been in charge, things haven't quite gone to plan for the midfielder.

He did win the Premier League title with the club during the 2024-25 campaign but, the season after, he was shipped out on loan to Aston Villa where he failed to meet expectations and only featured in nine games.

This term, the same thing has happened again as, even though he's one of Valencia's highest-paid players, he's not met the standards expected of him.

Elliott's lack of form has caused all sorts of rumours to emerge with journalist German Munoz now sharing an update on the Englishman's current situation.

"Valencia’s winter transfer window situation. Braulio has no plans to overhaul the squad by moving out key players, but he will try to offload players who get little playing time to free up more room for signings," he wrote.

"Elliot: very high wages; if his level doesn’t improve, there is a possibility of terminating his loan in January if Liverpool agree."

Harvey Elliott must do everything he can to get his Liverpool career back on track

Elliott's career started off with so much expectation but, right now, it feels like he's plateauing.

Indeed, he did manage to have a rather impressive Euros with England's Under-21's last summer but, that clearly wasn't enough.

This season-long loan with Valencia is probably the last chance that Elliott is going to get to prove his worth to Liverpool.

If Elliott doesn't turn things around soon, it's hard to see what his next step will be, so, here's hoping that he can replicate his recent Copa del Rey performance in the future.

#1588. Germany vs Netherlands - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 14 Nov 2026 23:59, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 04:46

Fighting for a place in the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals, Germany are set to host League A's Group A2 leaders, the Netherlands, at Olympiastadion Berlin on Monday.

Die Mannschaft know that they likely need to win to progress, while Oranje are through barring an unprecedented swing in goal-difference.

Jurgen Klopp's Germany are pushing to qualify for the Nations League quarter-finals for just the second time, but they face a tough test to reach the last eight.

Die Mannschaft are currently third in Group A2, level on eight points with Greece and three behind the Netherlands, and their chance to go through leans on the fact UEFA prioritises head-to-head points between tied teams.

Klopp's side were beaten 1-0 by the Azure and White on September 27 before drawing 0-0 with them on matchday four.

However, Ivan Jovanovic's men were hammered 7-0 by the Dutch on Friday, meaning that a German victory over the Netherlands on Monday would see them progress ahead of Greece regardless of their result against Serbia.

Die Mannschaft were held to a 1-1 stalemate by Oranje on matchday one, with Cody Gakpo equalising in second-half stoppage time to deny his former Liverpool manager maximum points.

Klopp's team have remained undefeated in the group since their loss to Greece, most recently beating Serbia 3-1 on Friday, when they raced into a 2-0 lead within the first 14 minutes thanks to an own-goal from Srdjan Babic and a follow-up by Florian Wirtz.

Meanwhile, Xavi's Netherlands have yet to taste defeat in the Nations League this term, and are in a commanding position at the top of their group going into the final matchday.

Leading with 11 points, Oranje's 7-0 demolition of Greece last time out - following a 2-2 draw on October 1 - means the only possibility of them finishing below the top two is if there is a dramatic 14-goal swing in the Azure and White's favour.

Xavi is without talismanic centre-back Virgil van Dijk this month, but his team were still able to keep their first clean sheet in the competition on Friday, while Tijani Reijnders's first-half hat-trick set the tone at the opposite end of the pitch.

However, it remains to be seen whether the Netherlands can repeat that attacking showcase in Germany, considering that they have won just one of their last six away clashes against Die Mannschaft.

On the other hand, Oranje are unbeaten in their past seven matches on the road, and last suffered a travelling defeat in a penalty shootout against Spain during the Nations League quarter-finals in March 2025, following a 5-5 aggregate draw.

Germany have no new injury issues to contend with, though they are missing Bayern Munich stars Jamal Musiala and Serge Gnabry due to respective muscle problems.

In their absence, Klopp could continue with Brajan Gruda, Florian Wirtz and Derry Scherhant behind Arsenal man Kai Havertz up top.

As for the Netherlands, they were forced to take off Frenkie De Jong at half time against Greece after he suffered back pain, and he has now left the national squad to return to Barcelona.

Teun Koopmeiners looks set to step in and fill the gap alongside Joey Veerman at the base of Xavi's midfield, while Tijani Reijnders operates in the number 10 role.

Further forward, Donyell Malen has been a standout for Roma this season with 12 goals across all competitions, and he will be keen to add to his goal against Greece while Cody Gakpo and Crysencio Summerville provide width.

Captain Virgil van Dijk has sat out this international break with complaints of physical discomfort, so expect to see Tottenham Hotspur's Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke start at centre-back.

Ter Stegen; Treu, Thiaw, Tah, Mittelstadt; Kimmich, Pavlovic; Gruda, Wirtz, Scherhant; Havertz

Verbruggen; Dumfries, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Timber; Veerman, Koopmeiners; Summerville, Reijnders, Gakpo; Malen

The maths of the table may be complex, but Germany know that a simple victory will see them through to the quarter-finals.

Oranje have yet to lose in the Nations League this season, though with the stakes lowered, they could be caught off guard.

#1587. Report: Liverpool veteran eyed by Euro club as Anfield reunion edges closer

Liverpool have a lot of tough decisions to make ahead of the January transfer window.

A handful of their players have their contracts expiring this summer which means that, from January, they'll be able to talk to clubs outside of England about a potential move.

And, if they reach an agreement with a club on terms that they're happy with, they can accept the deal and there will be nothing that Liverpool can do about it.

So, the sooner Liverpool figure out which of their players they want to keep, the better.

Virgil van Dijk is now wanted on a free transfer by Trabzonspor

Virgil van Dijk is probably the highest-rated Liverpool player who's contract expires in June 2027.

The Dutchman has been the rock in the centre of the Reds' defence for as long as anyone can remember with fans unable to imagine a Liverpool squad without him among it.

His performances alone have often won the Reds games and, he's single-handedly earned them points thanks to his aerial prowess.

Obviously, there have been one or two occasions this term when he's made the odd mistake but, he's still, without question, the Reds' best centre-back.

But, since he's now 35 years old, questions are being asked about whether he can keep this level of form up over the next couple of years with this being one of the main reasons why a new contract hasn't been agreed for him yet.

This lack of decisiveness has led to many different clubs from across the globe showing an interest in signing him with La Gazetta dello Sport now throwing another team into the ring.

"Van Dijk isn't just a Cardinale fan, but also Zlatan Ibrahimovic," they wrote.

"There's a connection between giants. Obviously, however, there's no shortage of admirers even far from Milan.

"Starting with Turkish clubs (Galatasaray, Fenerbahçe, and Trabzonspor, with Momo Salah eager to reunite with his former teammate on the Bosphorus) and Saudi Arabia.

"Van Dijk turns 36 on July 8th, and his next contract will likely be the last of his career, or thereabouts. If his priority is money, AC Milan will inevitably have an uphill battle.

"Conversely, if Virgil wants to pursue his childhood passions, the Rossoneri jersey could be one of the most desirable opportunities.

Liverpool can't let Virgil van Dijk leave without having a replacement lined up

As mentioned, Van Dijk is literally the heart of Liverpool's defence.

Without him, the club would be nowhere near as good as they are now and, would almost certainly be residing outside of the Champions League spots.

But, with the Dutchman now entering the twilight stages of his career, it's clear to see why questions are being asked about his future.

If the Reds do decide to call it quits with their captain, they must have a replacement lined up for him because, as good as Jeremy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni are, neither of them can be expected to fill Van Dijk's shoes yet.

Both defenders are still in the early stages of their careers and, right now, Leoni still hasn't even returned from his ACL tear he suffered at the start of last season.

Centre-backs such as Nico Schlotterbeck, Jacobo Ramon and Finn Jeltsch have all been linked as potential options to explore but, as of right now, nothing concrete has laid out.

If Van Dijk does leave Liverpool and ends up becoming Mohamed Salah's teammate again, one of these players needs to turn into a concrete interest and the Reds must figure out what their plans are.

Because, at the moment, it feels like their defence is in a bit of disarray, especially since Ronald Araujo is only on a season long loan and will be exiting Anfield in June 2027.

The favourites are clear, though: Endrick and Nicolo Tresoldi.

Speaking on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, Matteo Moretto provided an update on the Rossoneri’s pursuit for both forwards and whether either was progressing, as MilanNews relayed.

“Although Mourinho continues to say that Endrick will stay at Real Madrid, the truth is that the player has the ball right now. #1585. Central African Republic vs Benin - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 14 Nov 2026 23:59

Central African Republic host Benin at the Japoma Stadium in Douala, Cameroon, on Monday in the fourth round of Group F in 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying.

Benin won the first leg 4-1 in Abidjan on Thursday and lead Group F on goal difference, level on seven points with Burkina Faso, while Central African Republic remain bottom with no points and a goal difference of -6.

Central African Republic, known as Les Fauves, have lost all three qualifiers, scoring two goals and conceding eight, and have not won any match since October last year.

Mauritania won 3-1 in their opener on September 24, and Burkina Faso followed with a 1-0 victory over them on September 28.

Head coach Abdelaziz Kerkache, a Moroccan who has previously worked at Mouloudia d’Oujda, was appointed on November 6 to replace Eloge Enza Yamissi, only six days before the first leg.

Kerkache recalled Geoffrey Kondogbia of Olympique de Marseille and Le Mans forward Louis Mafouta, who both missed the opening two qualifiers, and Mafouta responded by equalising in the first leg.

Les Fauves had more of the ball in Abidjan, with 56% possession and eight corners to Benin’s five, yet goalkeeper Dominique Youfeigane faced eight shots on target and conceded four.

Central African Republic are still chasing a first Africa Cup of Nations finals appearance after narrowly missing out in 2021 and 2023, and their home leg is being staged in Douala rather than in Bangui.

Benin, nicknamed Les Guepards, have taken seven points from three Group F games under Gernot Rohr, beginning with a 1-1 draw at Burkina Faso on September 25.

A 2-1 win over Mauritania in Abidjan on September 29 followed, with Rodolfo Aloko scoring either side of half time, as Benin again used an Ivory Coast venue because the Stade de l’Amitie in Cotonou is not yet approved for qualifiers.

Hassane Imourane opened the scoring in the seventh minute of the first leg, Louis Mafouta equalised in the 19th, and Benin were 3-1 up at half time after Aloko struck in the 31st minute and Aiyegun Tosin in the 36th.

Tosin completed his brace in the 56th minute, and he and Aloko have now scored six of Benin’s seven goals in qualifying.

Benin won despite having only 44% of the possession, turning 18 shots into four goals, with eight efforts on target against Central African Republic’s 14 shots and five on target.

Rohr said afterwards that the scoreline flattered his side because Central African Republic attacked a great deal, and he expects a reaction in a rematch only four days later.

Central African Republic Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Central African Republic form (all competitions):

Benin Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

For the Central African Republic, Edwin Quarshie, booked in the 1-0 defeat by Burkina Faso, missed the first leg through suspension for accumulated yellow cards and should be available again on Monday.

Venuste Baboula, who has an ankle sprain, was left out of the starting lineup on Thursday, and he could be saved for the return match.

Kondogbia, Mafouta and Goduine Koyalipou all started in Abidjan, and Kerkache has had only one match to work with that group.

For Benin, captain and striker Steve Mounie remains out injured, so Rohr again leans on Aloko, Tosin and Junior Olaitan, who has three goals and seven assists for Besiktas this season.

Parfait Faton, a 16-year-old midfielder from AAS Sarcelles, received his first senior call-up in a 25-player squad that also includes Sessi D’Almeida and Jodel Dossou.

Central African Republic possible starting lineup:

Youfeigane; Yangao, Kouadio, Gambor, Yapende; Solet, Kondogbia, Diomande; Yawenendji, Koyalipou, Mafouta

Dandjinou; T. Ouorou, Roche, Tijani, Azongnitode; D’Almeida, Imourane; Aloko, Olaitan, Y. Ouorou; Tosin

Benin were far more efficient than their numbers suggest, putting eight of 18 shots on target with only 44% of the ball, and they did it without Mounie.

Central African Republic have conceded eight goals in three qualifiers, and a second game in four days under Kerkache is unlikely to repair a defence that let in three before half time on Thursday.

Benin cannot afford to slip either, because Burkina Faso are also on seven points after an added-time winner from Elohim Kabore against Mauritania, and the Cheetahs lead the table only on goal difference.

A clean sheet is less certain, because Mafouta equalised in the first leg and Kondogbia gives Les Fauves a better platform than they had in September, so we expect Central African Republic to score but not to take anything from the game.

#1584. Opinion: Liverpool will solve long-standing problem with move for La Liga star

Liverpool's fans probably thought that their team would be set in stone for a good while after they'd spent over £600 million on new players across the last couple of seasons.

However, that has not been exactly how things have gone.

Right now, the Reds are fourth in the Premier League table and have even lost a Champions League game against Fenerbahce.

This obviously wasn't in Andoni Iraola's plans when he took over as the Liverpool head coach but, for now, that's the way things seem to be headed.

But, since the transfer window is now just over a month away from opening again, the rumour mill is beginning to go into overdrive with the perfect opportunity for Liverpool to explore now emerging.

Barcelona want to sign Pedro Porro which could open the door for a Liverpool deal

Liverpool's defence was their main focus during the summer window.

Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo were brought in and have both instantly made a massive difference to the Reds' fortunes.

However, with so many changes still likely to take place at Anfield before the 2027-28 season kicks off, the futures of many players are still unknown.

This lack of knowing hasn't stopped players from being linked with Liverpool with a new player reportedly on their radar every day.

And, while the Reds may have made an enquiry to Tottenham about signing Pedro Porro, the Spaniard isn't the player who Liverpool may have just been given the green light to sign.

"Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester City have all made enquiries about Tottenham Hotspur right-back Pedro Porro, but the Spanish international has his heart set on a return to LaLiga, TEAMtalk can reveal," TEAMtalk wrote.

"The three Premier League giants are all assessing their options at full-back and have asked about Porro after becoming aware that he could be available for the right price.

"However, TEAMtalk understands the defender’s preference is to return to Spain, with both Barcelona and Real Madrid having made clear their admiration for the 27-year-old.

"Porro enjoyed an outstanding World Cup finals campaign, as TEAMtalk has previously revealed, further enhancing his reputation and attracting interest from some of Europe’s biggest clubs.

"Chelsea are exploring potential additions at right-back, with Malo Gusto a possible January departure, while Liverpool and Manchester City also recognise the need to improve their options despite having players available in the position.

"Porro has emerged as an attractive target for all three, but sources close to the situation indicate that his camp are firmly focused on the interest from Spain."

Barcelona signing Pedro Porro could allow Alejandro Balde to join Liverpool

Full-back has been a major problem area for ages now at Liverpool.

From the very moment Trent Alexander-Arnold chose to pack his bags and leave for free, the Reds haven't had the best of luck.

Since then, Andy Robertson has also exited and, both Jeremie Frimpong and Conor Bradley have spent more time injured than they have playing.

That's why so many full-backs have been linked with a Liverpool move over the last couple of years.

And now, if Porro joins Barcelona, the Reds could be handed their best chance ever to sign their perfect full-back in Alejandro Balde.

The Spaniard has been put up for sale by the La Liga outfit and, if Hansi Flick asks to sign Porro too, Balde will fall even further down the pecking order.

A fee worth around £34 million is all that Barca want for the 23-year-old and, since he already has so much experience in the Champions League and La Liga, he'd probably be able to fit straight into Iraola's plans at left-back or right-back.

This would be ideal for Liverpool and would help them solve one of their main issues from the last few years.

#1583. Tare discusses new Milan direction, limitations in his role and ‘jealousy’: “Better late than never”

Igli Tare has spoken without holding anything back about his time at AC Milan, explaining his frustration with several things.

When Tare arrived, many Milan fans were happy to see someone with Serie A experience oversee the project and whilst his first season didn’t end how anyone had hoped, he wasn’t seen as a major issue.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

So, when it was announced that he was part of a complete overturning of the management, there was a bit of a surprise, even if it did feel inevitable at one point.

With the overhaul of changes in the summer, one does wonder what Tare would have done differently, especially with suggestions that his hands were tied in the mercato last season. Nevertheless,

Speaking on Sky Sport’s ‘Calcio Unplugged’, Igli Tare revealed all to Gianluca Di Marzio and Stefano Borghi in an in-depth interview about his time with the Diavolo, as Radio Rossonera has relayed.

“Today is the first time I’ve spoken out after all these months. The wound of not having reached the Champions League is still enormous, and since I arrived at Milan – also questioning myself with the type of contract I signed – the objective couldn’t be only the Champions League; otherwise I wouldn’t have understood where I was.”

“It was great because he was the one who convinced me. He had such a huge desire to join Milan. I wanted to video chat before going to see him because I couldn’t believe it. But after five minutes, I knew in my head that he was the player Milan really lacked.

“Not just because of his qualities, but as a man and as a figure that that team didn’t have. He never said no. A photo with a child, an autograph, a meeting, talking to someone… He never said no. These are the things that humility is key to in life.

“I’m proud to have brought a great champion to Milan. In my opinion, if he wants, he can play another two seasons without any problem. He never missed a training session. Sometimes we were the ones to stop him because he was always there, ready. Loving football at that age is truly an honour.”

Is it a characteristic of the champion or is it a generational issue? Today’s champions seem to have a different mentality:

“Today we live in the age of social media. At 16, you’re already a footballer who can earn millions of euros. Living this way, you have the problem of not only managing a player, who is still a child, but you have to manage the business they bring with them: family, agents, girlfriends…

“These are obstacles that didn’t exist back then. We were a generation that played in the streets. Back then, our parents beat us to get us to come home. Today, however, it’s to get them out of the house because they spend all day in front of computers.

“This aspect has been lost a bit, but it’s our fault. Education and discipline are the key to success.”

Fullkrug. He performed poorly in Milan, but in the Bundesliga he’s scoring a lot and is the top scorer. How do you explain that?

“It’s simple. He came to us after a tough time in England, with a lot of scepticism. And then, right away, he broke his toe. No one ever said he’d been having injections on the bone for two months just to train, let alone to play.

“I knew he was a centre forward that the team was missing; given his characteristics and his interpretation of the game, his qualities were unquestionable. Just two years before coming to Milan, he’d played in the Champions League final, playing a key role in a competition with Borussia Dortmund.

“There are situations where, for a player, even a very important one, it matters how you feel. If you feel appreciated, valued, taken into consideration… When you play for a club like Milan, the weight of the shirt is completely different than when you play for other clubs.

“You feel it from the first day you join. I had no doubt that he could be what he’s demonstrating now.”

“We tried to sign him back in June. We made a first attempt. In the final days of the transfer window, another important name we tried to sign was Akanji. The Champions League was crucial for both of them. They turned him down, not because of the club’s importance, but because he wasn’t playing in the Champions League.

“Then the opportunity arose again at the end of August for Rabiot. Defeat against Cremonese? No, we had already decided to bring him. It was just a matter of contract details.”

“It was difficult for us because we decided to change the formation five days before the transfer window closed. Switching from a 4-3-3 to a three-man defense meant we were having a really hard time finding a quality player in the last five days.

“We were a bit unlucky, first with the Akanji story and then with Liverpool’s Joe Gomez… Guehi’s move from Crystal Palace to Liverpool fell through, and at the last minute they—we already had the deal ready, we were just waiting for this to happen—made a step back. And to avoid being left without a central defender at the last minute, we signed Odogu as a promising player.”

On not being able to reach the Champions League and not being able to continue his work at Milan…

“This is the first time today, after all these months, that I’ve spoken about this… The wound of not reaching the Champions League is still enormous. I think that from the first day I arrived at Milan, even in the way I signed—I questioned myself with the type of contract.

“I said, ‘If I have to come only for the Champions League objective, then I don’t understand where I’ve come from.’ Milan has a different story. I had to go through a trial. The disappointment is that those who run the club didn’t understand how much time people needed, which is now being done, rightly so.

“That is to say, it takes several transfer sessions to get a competitive team ready to win. At the beginning, I felt the responsibility to put the pieces together immediately, because after the defeat in the Coppa Italia final the year before, there were some important signs.

“I didn’t know where to start. But I think we did an important job last summer, we sold for a lot and also signed 10 new players. Then you need time to integrate, learn new philosophies and create a cohesive group, hungry to win.

“Until March-April, we were a group with difficulties, but we were at the top of the table. Then in the last 10 matchdays, we had a mental breakdown, also due to other external dynamics, which I don’t want to discuss here, which had a significant impact.

“Internal or external dynamics? External to the team. But we also have some blame: myself first and foremost, along with Max [Allegri].

“We had to be a little more attentive to certain dynamics. We needed to be more present with the team to ultimately lead them to the final result. Isolation is the wrong word; I don’t believe in these things. I believe in teamwork; I believe in cohesion: from the club to the team.

“When this happens, you transmit it to the team. When these situations become possible, you could also see it in the team’s results, because the players are very attentive. Sometimes we think they have other interests, but they pay attention to everything that comes out. They follow everything very carefully and transmit it.

“Instilling serenity… How can you convey serenity? When, in difficult moments, you show that you believe in the project more than before. Sometimes I missed this feeling, a lack of something that could give us the final push.”

But despite this, did you think you could continue? Does this farewell after only a year feel like a stab in the back?

“Look, I would have asked for a round table where we could all sit down together and analyze everything. Then they could have just said ‘no, thanks’… But I respect the decision they made. I accept it with great regret, but I’ve never questioned it because there’s someone above me who has to decide, including for the fate of the club.

“And when they decide to take a different path, you have to accept it. I know things could have gone differently, even much better. I’ll always be a Milan fan, even after an experience like that.”

Was AC Milan a team that needed the constant presence of a manager or coach to avoid letting itself go as it later did?

“The feeling I had at the beginning was that this leadership was a bit lacking. The arrival of Modric—and another of our goals was also Granit Xhaka, Leverkusen’s captain—was precisely to bring real players into the group, with important characteristics and capable of leading others.

“Granit didn’t arrive; Luka arrived, who has a different way of being a leader: he does it in silence and with his attitude on the pitch. I had the opportunity to meet Mike Maignan: an extraordinary guy, a soul who cares deeply about the AC Milan shirt.

“Gabbia is another extraordinary guy; he lives for this club. Rabiot too… His experience spoke for itself. The great disappointment is that I expected something more in terms of responsibility and leadership from Pulisic: he’s a top-class player with unquestionable qualities. But in terms of performance, things happened that I had never experienced in my career…

“Like Gimenez: an extraordinary guy with numbers that spoke for themselves; for a year he failed to score a goal. Then it happened that Pulisic didn’t score for six months. He scored a goal. Then Leao didn’t score for four months.

“Situations that are hard to come by in football have happened… It can happen that you don’t score for a month, two months, but that long a period of time also affected the team’s final performance.

“Losing a match against Cagliari the way we did, 2-1, I think was the worst match of my life. The feeling and the disappointment I felt towards the fans in the stadium that night is something I will never forget for the rest of my life.”

If Cardinale had been the Cardinale he is today, the one who is also physically present, would you still be AC ​​Milan’s DS?

“I can’t answer that question; he has to answer it. I can say that I remember when the Jashari negotiations were going on… I had just landed in Rome and I was very pleased when he called me because he wanted to understand what was happening in that negotiation.

“I explained all the dynamics to him and I really liked that he said, ‘Anything you need, if you have to spend a little more, let me know because I’m here.’ Then during that process I never had the chance to talk to him, even intentionally.

“There were other people above me who I never wanted to bypass. I never had a direct relationship with him, and the possibility of a discussion would have helped everyone. Not me, but everyone. By putting all the problems and dynamics on the table, we could have resolved things much sooner. But I think it’s a new experience for Cardinale.

“He’s had experience in other sports in America. Now he’s done something important, taking responsibility and putting his face on the line. I would have preferred to have had that presence even when I was there because it would have been very useful. But for the Milan, better late than never.

“Now, for better or worse, he will make his own decisions and responsibilities. I think that for him, too, the best interests of Milan come first.”

Was Leao a problem or a resource in your mind?

“I knew him from the outside. When I had the chance to meet him in person, I thought he was an extraordinary guy. I truly loved him as a person, like everyone else. But he was the player from whom we all expected something more. I think football was no longer a priority for him. That’s the key to understanding him.”

“I think a bit about his life outside of football. Music, fashion, things… But I never doubted the sense of belonging he had towards Milan. You could sense that he loved playing for Milan and was suffering from not performing.

“He had many physical problems… First a calf, then a bit of pubalgia… He always played with his hands under control. I always tried to have individual conversations with him more than with any other Milan player.

“Every time I spoke to him, I left with a positive feeling. I sensed that he wanted to. But sometimes wanting isn’t enough.”

Was there a chance that Leao would leave during your summer too?

“A concrete offer never came for him. Regarding the other transfers, it’s not just Tare’s job. When I arrived – even at Lazio – I was a bit alone, but I tried to involve all the members of the club to give him the importance he needed to build a sense of belonging and responsibility. I think I did a very good job, together with Furlani, Ibra, and Moncada.

“We achieved significant sales figures, in a year when we weren’t even in the Champions League. Thanks to the work we did last summer, investments were made this year, with the money we had at the time. I really believe in teamwork.

“I said it even before the Coppa Italia match against Bari; I asked to speak to convey the importance of the work of the people within the club because it was right that way. Then afterwards, it’s human…

“They were coming off a bad year, when two cumbersome figures like Tare and Allegri arrive, and everyone was talking about Tare and Allegri, some disappointment was understandable. I understood the feeling they had, but I could… There was little to do about it.

“For me, it was a new path, a new opportunity. It was essential to work as a team and present ourselves as a real company.”

#1582. Opinion: Liverpool send clear message about future of £45m star

Liverpool have a lot of transfers to think about ahead of the January window.

The Anfield outfit are in desperate need of reinforcements and, without them, it's hard to see how they'll finish the season any higher in the Premier League than they currently find themselves.

Indeed, a fourth-place finish would mean that they'd still qualify for the Champions League but, with how much money they've spent on new players over the last couple of years, fans will have been expecting a lot more.

Right now, there's nothing that can be done until the January transfer window so, Andoni Iraola is just going to have to try his best to get his team to earn as many points as possible so that, by the new year, they all have a clear idea of what lies ahead for them.

Liverpool might not be signing Ronald Araujo permanently

Ronald Araujo has probably been Liverpool's most successful signing this season.

The Uruguayan was brought in as cover for centre-back and right-back but, he's ended up making the right-back spot his own.

Last term, full-back was a major issue for Liverpool with the club ending up having to play Dominik Szoboszlai and Curtis Jones at right-back on multiple occasions.

So, to everyone looking at the Reds, it was clear that a new right-back was needed which is where Araujo came in.

And, even though he's been in fine form and hasn't ended up injured yet, this recent update from James Pearce has made fans question whether Liverpool are going to activate their option to buy or not.

"Centre-back not a priority for Liverpool so highly unlikely they will invest heavily in that area either in Jan or next summer. Jacquet has made a huge impact and big hopes for fellow young CBs Leoni, Ndukwe and Ndiaye," he shared via X.

Liverpool are making a big mistake by not wanting to sign Ronald Araujo permanently

As mentioned, Araujo has easily been one of Liverpool's best players this season.

The 27-year-old has helped shore up the Reds' back line massively and, without him, Liverpool would be in some serious trouble.

Indeed, his injury history and age are both a tad concerning but, in reality, it's hard to see how Iraola and Julian Ward are going to get a better deal than the £45.9 million option to buy they have for the Barcelona captain.

Of course, some younger players could be signed for less of a fee but, it's Araujo's years of experience that set him apart from other candidates.

If the Reds were serious about making Araujo's deal permanent, talks would probably already be underway.

However, since that isn't the case, fans may need to prepare themselves to say goodbye to the defender in the near future.

#1581. Fabrizio Romano confirms Liverpool stance on Trent Alexander-Arnold

Trent Alexander-Arnold's exit last season was expected.

When the Englishman failed to sign a new deal after the January transfer window slammed shut, fans sort of accepted that it was the end of his time at L4.

Liverpool wanted to keep hold of their right-back with Richard Hughes making multiple offers to try and retain his services.

However, he chose against cementing his legacy as a Liverpool legend and instead chose to try and make his mark at Real Madrid.

One of the reasons behind this was so that he could start challenging for the Ballon D'Or but, since Federico Valverde is now being chosen over him at right-back, that clearly hasn't worked out as he'd have wanted it to.

His lack of appearances have caused many rumours to start emerging with a return to Liverpool even being discussed.

Fabrizio Romano confirms there has been no contact between Liverpool and Trent Alexander-Arnold

If Alexander-Arnold chose to stay at Liverpool, he'd still probably be one of the first names on their team sheet.

His style of play was perfectly suited to the Reds and, since Andoni Iraola likes his full-backs to attack, he'd have fit straight into the Spaniard's plans as well.

Instead, he left Arne Slot without a natural right-back for most of the season thanks to the many injuries that Jeremie Frimpong and Conor Bradley suffered, and, he also forced Iraola to bring Ronald Araujo in.

Of course, Araujo has done fairly well since joining Liverpool but, since he's only on a season-long loan, his future is still undecided.

Each of these reasons are why the Reds have been linked with their former star once again.

And now, transfer guru Fabrizio Romano has shared an update on how Liverpool and the Englishman feel about linking up once again.

“Today, we focus on the future of Trent Alexander-Arnold,” Romano said.

“[There have been] many rumours and many stories over the recent weeks about the possibility for Trent to leave Real Madrid already in the January transfer window.

“And, some links coming from England about a potential return to Liverpool.

“Let’s immediately clarify one thing, there is zero ongoing between Trent Alexander-Arnold, Real Madrid and Liverpool, zero at all.

“Trent obviously respects and loves the club but that’s it, it’s in the past. Trent is fully focused on Real Madrid and there is no contact or negotiation at all with Liverpool.”

Trent Alexander-Arnold returning to Liverpool would be massive

Although the way that things ended between Alexander-Arnold and Liverpool wasn't ideal, his return would still be massive for the Reds.

The Anfield outfit are in desperate need of some creativity because, right now, Florian Wirtz just isn't cutting it.

Of course, he has been fairly unlucky during his time at Anfield thus far but, even with that taken into account, you'd still be expecting him to perform much better, especially with Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak ahead of him.

Alexander-Arnold has been left out of Jose Mourinho's plans for a while now and, even though the Special One keeps saying that he'll get his chance, that doesn't feel all that likely.

So, the fact that Liverpool and the Englishman aren't in contact with one another is fairly upsetting, especially since these are supposed to be the prime years of his career when he should be playing every single game possible.

#1580. “Important to take time” – Gabbia admits January return is possible with right precautions

Matteo Gabbia has admitted that he could return to the field in January for AC Milan, but he doesn’t want to rush back.

It has been a difficult season for Milan, at least where injuries are concerned. In defence, they have had issues reminiscent of the 2023/24 season, where Gabbia had to be brought back from his loan spell at Villarreal.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This season, though, it seems Gerry Cardinale is going to go down a different route and spend to help Ruben Amorim with his defensive options. Indeed, there have been plenty of rumours about recruitments at the back.

However, Gabbia could again be a key returnee in January, with him hoping to return from injury early in the new year.

Speaking to Sky Sport (via MilanNews) – at an event organised by the Milan Foundation at Milan’s “Arturo Toscanini” secondary school, where they met with several children with disabilities – Gabbia discussed the importance of the event, as well as his recovery.

“It’s wonderful, very enjoyable to spend hours with them. It’s also beautiful to see how they manage to create a group, something that really shows the importance of teamwork, the importance of friendship, even among themselves.

“We’re happy; we thank Fondazione Milan for the project, which is always beautiful and important: we’re happy to be a part of it and we’re enjoying the afternoon.”

Are you able to rejoin the group in January?

“Yes, that could be the time: we’re trying to work hard and do everything as best we can. I obviously have to thank the physiotherapists and the doctor because we’re really doing everything we can every day to try to heal the injury and get back on the pitch feeling good.

“It’s definitely been an unlucky season for me so far: I don’t want it to happen again or for any recurrences, so it’s also important to take the right time, get back in shape, and support the team right now.”

“Although it’s bad for the team that there are so many injured players, we’re together right now, supporting each other and trying to encourage each other through therapy, gym work, and the entire recovery process. Therefore, we’re trying to work as a team this week too, to overcome all the players’ injuries.

“From a personal standpoint, I’m trying to take this time calmly, in the sense that these things are part of sport, part of life, and not all moments are the same.

“This is certainly a difficult time, but it still allows me to stay close to the team, to try to lend my support, even in the good and bad times. That’s what I’m doing, in addition to obviously doing what I can to try to return as soon as possible and make my contribution on the pitch.”

How do you explain the team’s ups and downs?

“I think it’s something we need to get our heads around; we need to understand the importance of every game.

“The other day I heard our coach give an interview in which he said something important: we need to understand that every game, when you don’t win, is taken as a defeat, a heavy defeat. We need to truly understand the importance of every game and approach training to prepare 100%, as best as possible, for every match.

“Therefore, I think this is room for improvement, but I see a group that is really eager to improve, to work, and as a result, I’m sure we’ll be able to fix this flaw as well.

“Although we’ve had a good start to the year in the league and less so in the Europa League, we have plenty of time to improve and have a strong year.”

#1579. Iceland vs Luxembourg - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 15 Nov 2026 00:03, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 03:16

Iceland will look to wrap up automatic promotion when they welcome Luxembourg to Reykjavik for Monday's Nations League encounter.

The hosts are sitting two points at the top of Group C4, while the visitors are languishing at the bottom of the standings ahead of the final matchday of the league phase.

After being relegated from League B in 2024-25, Iceland have put in a strong performance in their first-ever League C campaign, collecting 11 points from a possible 15.

After playing out a 1-1 draw with Estonia, Arnar Gunnlaugsson's side recorded back-to-back 3-0 victories over Luxembourg and Bulgaria.

However, their momentum was somewhat halted by a goalless draw against Estonia in their final outing of the September/October international break.

But they certainly had no issues troubling the scorers in Friday's emphatic 5-0 away win over Iceland, which came courtesy of an Andri Gudjohnsen hat-trick, an Orri Oskarsson effort and an own goal.

Gudjohnsen, who is now the leading scorer in League C with five goals, has helped his country secure a playoff berth and put them in pole position to secure automatic promotion on the final matchday.

With a two-point advantage over Estonia, Iceland know a win would guarantee a first-place finish, while a draw would likely be enough due to their significant goal difference advantage.

They would even progress with a defeat if Estonia fail to beat Bulgaria, but they will certainly fancy their chances of taking all three points, considering they are currently League C's highest scorers and have recorded shutouts in each of their last five matches.

Luxembourg are competing in their fourth consecutive League C campaign, knowing they will remain in the third tier no matter the result in Monday's trip to the Icelandic capital.

That is because they are six points adrift of the top two after each of their last four matches since beating Bulgaria 2-1 on matchday one.

In fact, they have failed to trouble the scorers in each of those four defeats, including another goal-shy display in Friday's narrow 1-0 home loss against Estonia, leaving them one point behind third-placed Bulgaria.

That result made it three consecutive home losses without troubling the scorers since Luxembourg won 3-0 against Malta in the second leg of their Nations League relegation/promotion playoff tie in March.

As they head on their travels for Monday's fixture, Jeff Strasser's side can take confidence from the fact they have won three of their last four away internationals, although their most recent away outing resulted in a 1-0 defeat against Estonia.

If they were to win on Monday, it would represent their first-ever away victory over Iceland and just their second head-to-head success at any venue after winning 3-1 in a European Championship qualifier in September 2023.

Iceland will be unable to call upon Stefan Teitur Thordarson and Kristall Mani Ingason, who were forced in the first half against Bulgaria.

Hordur Magnusson replaced Thordarson in the ninth minute in Plovdiv, but he will miss Monday’s fixture through suspension after picking up his second yellow card of the league phase.

As a result of those absences, Gunnlaugsson has decided to call up Hjortur Hermannsson, Brynjar Ingi Bjarnason and Saevar Atli Magnusson.

As for the visitors, Omar Natami will serve a one-match ban after collecting his second yellow card of the league phase in the narrow loss to Estonia.

In positive news, Dirk Carlson is back from suspension and is expected to slot into central defence for Monday’s away fixture.

Enes Mahmutovic and Enzo dos Santos are also pushing for starting spots after coming off the bench to play over 30 minutes in Friday’s defeat.

Valdimarsson; Palsson, Gunnarsson, Gretarsson, Tomasson; Ellertsson, Johannesson, Haraldsson, Sigurdsson; Oskarsson, Gudjohnsen

Moris; Bohnert, Selimovic, Mahmutovic, Carlson; Olesen; V Thill, Dos Santos, Cruz, Kadamani; Dardari

Iceland will be full of confidence after thrashing Bulgaria 5-0 last time out, and we think they will produce another free-scoring display against a Luxembourg side that are low on confidence after four consecutive defeats.

#1574. Man City guilty: Erling Haaland "answers" contract decision after verdict as Enzo Maresca faces January transfer problem

By Lewis Nolan | 15 Nov 2026 01:29

Manchester City striker Erling Haaland has defended his choice to remain at Manchester City amid the fallout of their guilty verdict.

The Citizens were found guilty by an independent panel in September of breaching the Premier League's financial rules on an industrial scale.

A punishment has not yet been handed down, but there are fears among those associated with the club that sanctions could be as harsh as demotion.

It would be understandable if some players felt let down by City, who often expressed confidence that they would win their case.

Haaland revealed that he had no regrets about joining the club in 2022 and signing a new contract last year, telling TV2: "I assume the answers will come. I don’t know when. I haven’t read much about it. To be completely honest, I’m focused on trying to perform for Manchester City.

"A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022, and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. I think that says everything about the matter. I’m a City player and I’m incredibly happy there. I’d say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022.

"We can all agree on that. I would say so myself when I look at the trophies I’ve won and how I’ve developed on and off the pitch. I’m standing here after winning an international 3-1 and we're in the 1st seed pot for the Euro qualifiers. Things aren’t going so well for City in the league but we’ll try and turn that around against Fulham."

Haaland signed a new contract until 2034 in January 2025, though it is not clear if he would seek a move away from the club should they be severely punished.

City could win an appeal later this year, but the likelihood of the club overturning their guilty verdict is reportedly small.

A demotion to the Championship or lower divisions raises the possibility of a mass exodus, especially if the players have clauses in their contracts that make exits easier in the event of relegation.

Haaland is arguably the best striker in the world, and the 26-year-old will not want to spend at least a year of his prime competing for promotion.

It would not be surprising if the likes of Phil Foden or Nico O'Reilly opted to stay at the Etihad given they came through the academy, but it is hard to see others such as Haaland remaining a City player.

City currently find themselves third in the Premier League table, with the team trailing Arsenal by six points after 10 matchweeks.

Enzo Maresca will no doubt be targeting the January transfer window as an opportunity to strengthen in order to close the gap to the Gunners.

However, potential targets may be reluctant about joining the club due to the real threat of sanctions, and that would make a title challenge difficult.

Crystal Palace are reportedly determined to keep Ismaïla Sarr beyond the January transfer window, with discussions over a new contract offering fresh hope that the winger will remain at Selhurst Park.

The Senegal international attracted significant attention during the summer, including reported interest from Liverpool and Galatasaray.

Although Palace rejected approaches for the 28-year-old, questions have continued over his future following a difficult start to the season.

According to ⁠Football Insider, Palace have held positive discussions with Sarr over a potential contract extension and are hopeful of reaching an agreement.

The club reportedly view the winger as an important part of manager Pierre Sage’s plans and are reluctant to consider offers in January.

That stance follows a summer in which Liverpool reportedly made an offer worth around £50 million for Sarr. Palace ultimately kept hold of the forward, while interest from Turkey and the Saudi Pro League has continued.

A new contract could help Palace protect their position and discourage potential suitors from pursuing a move in the coming months. However, an agreement has not yet been confirmed.

Galatasaray remain one of the clubs to watch, having reportedly made an approach for Sarr during the summer transfer window.

Football Insider reports that the Turkish club could revisit their interest in January, particularly if the winger continues to struggle for regular playing time at Palace.

Sarr has endured a slow start to the campaign and has also dealt with fitness issues. His limited involvement has fuelled speculation about his future, although Palace are reportedly not allowing his recent lack of minutes to change their longer-term plans.

Liverpool were also linked with a move during the summer, but a January transfer to Anfield remains uncertain.

#1571. Barcelona chasing £50 million Brighton defender as Real Madrid and Liverpool join race

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Barcelona are reportedly keeping a close eye on Brighton & Hove Albion defender Luka Vuskovic, with the Croatian centre-back attracting interest from several of Europe’s biggest clubs.

The 19-year-old has made a strong impression since arriving at the Amex Stadium, and his performances have reportedly placed him on Barcelona’s radar ahead of a potential transfer battle next summer.

However, the Catalan giants face competition from Real Madrid and Liverpool, while Bayern Munich and Chelsea have also been monitoring his progress.

According to ⁠TEAMtalk, Barcelona have been tracking Vuskovic since last season and remain interested in securing his services.

The Croatian defender joined Brighton from Tottenham Hotspur in a deal worth up to £50 million during the summer, following an impressive loan spell with German side Hamburg.

Since moving to England, Vuskovic has established himself as a regular starter and strengthened his reputation through his aerial ability, physical presence and composure in possession.

Barcelona’s reported interest reflects their focus on identifying young defenders who could strengthen the backline for years to come. At just 19, Vuskovic has considerable room to develop further.

However, there is no indication that Barcelona have submitted a formal offer, with any concrete move reportedly more likely to take place next summer than in January.

Barcelona will not have a clear path to the defender’s signature.

Real Madrid and Liverpool are also reportedly seriously interested, while Bayern Munich have followed Vuskovic since his time in Germany. Chelsea remain another potential contender as they assess their defensive options.

Liverpool’s interest is particularly notable because of uncertainty surrounding Virgil van Dijk’s long-term future, with the Dutch defender’s contract approaching its final months. Vuskovic could potentially become a long-term option at the heart of Liverpool’s defence.

Real Madrid, meanwhile, are continuing to monitor one of European football’s most promising young centre-backs.

The competition could make a future transfer expensive, especially given Brighton’s strong negotiating position.

Brighton have little immediate reason to part ways with Vuskovic. The club invested a reported fee of up to £50 million to bring him in from Tottenham and secured his services on a contract running until 2031.

His rapid adaptation to the Premier League has made him an important part of Fabian Hürzeler’s plans, meaning Brighton are under no obvious pressure to sell.

A significant offer could eventually test their resolve, but any interested club would need to convince Brighton that losing such a highly rated young defender is worthwhile.
